title: Pre-hospital tranexamic acid in a rural emergency network: an audit of eligibility, administration and timing
abstract: Aim: to measure how many eligible injured adults receive pre-hospital tranexamic acid within three hours of injury in a rural ambulance service. Methods: audit of ambulance patient care records from January 2023 to June 2026 against the pathway standard, with second-reviewer checks of eligibility. Results and conclusions will be written after the audit; no outcome analysis is included.
introduction: Tranexamic acid reduces death from bleeding when given early, and the benefit falls with delay. Rural crews face long transport times and often work alone, and the network has never audited its pathway.
methods: Eligible incidents were identified from the ambulance records database; administration, dose time and injury time (known or estimated) were coded, with a second reviewer checking 10 percent of eligibility decisions. Results are proportions with confidence intervals by crew configuration, age and transport time.
results: No records have been reviewed yet. The report will present eligible incidents, the proportion treated within three hours, time to dose, doses outside protocol and documentation of injury time.
discussion: The discussion will describe where the pathway fails and what support might help, and will state that effects on survival cannot be judged without linked hospital data.
limitations: Record quality, estimated injury times and the absence of outcomes.
conclusion: To be written after the audit; it will be limited to compliance and timing.
summary: Audit-structured draft with results left empty; outcome analysis excluded until data sharing is renewed.
